# Repository working guidelines

Before working in this repository, consult the relevant guidance in `.junie/` and `docs/`.

- Check `.junie/` for applicable development rules and domain-specific guides. Follow the relevant guidelines when planning and implementing changes.
- When creating or editing a test file, keep every test in that file inside one `describe` block. If you touch a file whose tests are not grouped yet, wrap them all in one `describe` as part of that change.
- Place reusable utility/helper modules in an appropriate `utils/` directory rather than beside feature-specific files; create the scoped directory when needed and update imports.
- Use `docs/README.md` as the documentation index, then read the documents relevant to the task to understand the intended behavior and architecture.
- In card seed `params`, put printed keyword flags inside the `keywords` object (for example, `keywords: { quickStrike: true }`), never as top-level fields. `Card` in `packages/back/mc-back/src/model/printed/card.js` builds its `Keywords` from that object, so top-level keyword fields are ignored; add or update a runtime card-factory test when the keyword enables behavior.
- Implement Quickstrike according to `docs/02-08-KEYWORDS-STATUS.md` as a `ForcedResponseAbility` on `TRIGGER_ENGAGE_HERO`. Its eligibility depends on the engaged player being in hero form, not on the encounter minion's controller, because encounter minions are controlled by the scenario. For a revealed minion, defer that response until after its When Revealed abilities resolve.
- When adding or editing card abilities, consult `.junie/guidelines/translation-guide.md`, `.junie/guidelines/effects-guide.md`, and the relevant rules in `docs/02-06-ABILITIES-EFFECTS.md`.
- For scenario accessories attached to a Villain, follow the attachment bonus, keyword, Hero Action cost, and reflected-damage patterns in the [content-authoring skill](../mc-rrr-content-authoring/SKILL.md); test the applied modifier, real trigger context, and cleanup when the source leaves play.
- Add `LABEL_ATTACK` or `LABEL_THWART` only when the supplied card text explicitly includes the corresponding ability label (including localized equivalents); never infer either label from an effect or its targets.
- For defeat-related abilities, use the [defeat trigger selection table](../mc-rrr-content-authoring/SKILL.md#defeat-trigger-selection) to distinguish a card being defeated from that card defeating a minion.
- When configuring `EFFECT_FOR_EACH` exclusions, follow the [Effect target exclusions section](../mc-rrr-content-authoring/SKILL.md#effect-target-exclusions) and keep `.junie/guidelines/effects-guide.md` synchronized.
- Every configuration field named `target`, including `limit.target` and `maximum.target`, must use a `TARGET_*` constant, not a `PLACE_*`, `TIME_*`, or other namespace constant. Define `limit` and `maximum` scopes with `target`, never `time`. If no matching target constant exists, define a `TARGET_*` alias from the appropriate existing constant in `mc-shared/constants/targets.js`. Effect `params.target` values still need a resolver in `targetMap`; limit/maximum scope targets are metadata and need not resolve as effect selectors. A `limit` applies to its ability instance, while a `maximum` aggregates matching card names.
- Label every user-facing choice clearly: use `title` for effect options and `name` for `ABILITY_OPTION` abilities.
- When changing card, discard, or modal presentation, consult `.junie/guidelines/card-display-guide.md`.
- For enemy and scheme clicks, offer the player's basic attack or thwart only when the backend's legal-target check includes that exact card. Start a sole activation directly; when other available actions exist, put the basic activation first in the menu. Confirm with the acting superhero, selected target, and activation type, and support hiding future confirmations per player and match. Pass the selected target to the backend and revalidate it there; never turn an invalid target into an activation option.
- A stunned hero or ally may attempt a basic attack without a legal enemy target, and a confused hero or ally may attempt a basic thwart without a legal scheme target. Keep that basic action available in the actor's own ability menu when its target list is empty; do not invent a target. Pay the normal activation cost, including exhausting the actor, then remove the matching status instead of resolving the attack/thwart or its consequences. Preserve ordinary target selection when the player chooses a legal target. Add runtime tests for both statuses, empty targets, costs paid, status removal, and no attack/thwart resolution.
- Before serializing game state, finish calculations that can trigger effects or mutate displayed data; build the snapshot afterward. Keep incremental refreshes and full snapshots consistent, and test the first refresh after actions or identity flips without relying on a reload.
- Treat card text and structured data supplied by the user as the source of truth. Do not infer icons, attributes, traits, or effects from artwork; ask when an important rule interaction is ambiguous.
- For encounter cards, if the provided card text omits the printed boost-icon value, treat that value as 0. This does not omit or disable any separately specified Boost ability.
- Default boolean configuration and state to `false`; set a boolean to `true` only when explicitly required by the card text, rules, or user. Do not infer that a later scenario stage is final.
- For scenario abilities that grant persistent values while a card is in play, verify the granted value is applied to the actual character and stops applying when its source leaves play.
- For enemy activations with multiple boost cards, verify the activation resolves every card in dealt order and adds all printed boost values before calculating attack damage or scheme threat.
- For enemy attacks, abort the activation immediately when its attacker leaves play: do not continue attack steps or resolve attack-end triggers. Same-title Villain stage transitions continue with the new stage as the attacker; different-title transitions and a completed game stop the attack. Add runtime coverage for minion defeat, same-title continuation, different-title transition, and final Villain defeat.
- Apply the operator decision table in the effects guide before choosing a composition: periods preserve sentence order without creating a `Then` gate; independent effect clauses joined by `and` resolve simultaneously; `Then` gates on full resolution and belongs in `thenEffect`; if a preceding effect cannot resolve because its required target is not in play, its `Then` effect is not attempted; `instead` replaces rather than adds an effect; a comma alone has no timing meaning; `additional` modifies the effect it qualifies.
- For “if no attack occurred” or similar fallback clauses, put the attempted effect first in an `EFFECT_CHAINED`, then use `EFFECT_DO_IF` to inspect its actual result. Do not pre-check attacker/target presence: cancellation, stun, or another skipped resolution must also reach the fallback. Use `EFFECT_ENEMY_ATTACK` plus `{'effects.0.resolved': false}` for one attack, and `EFFECT_SEVERAL_ATTACKS` plus `{'effects.0.attacks.length': 0}` only for multiple attacks. Missing participants must leave a fresh unresolved result without throwing; add runtime tests for missing participants, canceled/status-skipped effects, and successful resolution. For analogous clauses about other effects, check the result property that represents the stated occurrence.
- Interpret “that/those” and “ese/a” as the specific target identified earlier in the text. Reuse that selection in the composition and dependent effects; do not prompt for an unrelated second target, and do not resolve the dependent effect when the original target cannot be selected.
- When a target count depends on a cost result, defer target selection until after the cost by configuring the generic multi-target parameter and calculating the count from the resolved cost data. The multi-target flag must not be treated as a card-specific branch or as a substitute for the count.
- When configured card or effect behavior reads runtime context paths (such as `paramsCalc`, `targetCountCalc`, `condition`, `effectCondition`, or `condition.exclude`), add a regression test that exercises the actual ability/effect with the runtime context shape and asserts the resulting behavior. A path-string assertion or a standalone `path()` test is not sufficient; follow `.junie/guidelines/effects-guide.md`.
- For `TRIGGER_THIS_ATTACK` responses conditioned on damage, use the `TakeDamageEffect` trigger payload (`effect.takenDamage` and `effect.selectedTarget`): the response window runs before `DealDamageEffect` copies damage to `attack.takenDamage`, and `effect.attacked` belongs to the enclosing attack effect rather than the damage payload. Add a runtime-context test using `TakeDamageEffect.getTriggersParams()` and cover zero damage and non-superhero targets; account for array-shaped damage in multi-target attacks.
- When an ability depends on which identity or character an event affects, gate it using the event target's full `name`; do not infer the identity from its owner or another character with a related name.
- When a card grants a stat bonus or keyword to a character named in its text, target the named character by `name`/identity across hero, alter-ego, and ally representations; do not infer the target from the source card's owner or controller. Name conditions on `TARGET_ALL_CHARACTERS` and `TARGET_ALL_FRIENDLY_CHARACTERS` match the active `name` or stable superhero `mainName`; if a multi-sided superhero matches by `mainName`, resolve the side whose full name was specified and keep the modifier limited to that side. Use `TARGET_YOUR_SUPERHERO` across both sides only when the text says "your superhero". For calculation-time numeric modifiers, gate the collector using the actual `effect.selectedTarget`.
- Use `EFFECT_CHAINED` for ordered or data-dependent steps and `EFFECT_SIMULTANEOUS` for independent effects joined by `and`; never assign an array directly to `ability.effect`. Consult `.junie/guidelines/targets-guide.md` when selecting or adding target selectors. Ensure each configured `ability.effect` resolves to one effect instance with a callable `canRun`.
- Keep general classes such as `Ability`, the base `Effect`, and factories free of branches for concrete cards or effect types. Put effect-specific parameter preparation in the concrete effect class and shared formula calculations in `Calc`.
- For `requiresPrePlayConfirmation`, set the boolean flag on the concrete effect and build its preview data and calculations in that effect's `confirmBeforeResolve()`. Reuse the same calculation used during resolution so the preview matches the applied result. Keep shared confirmation helpers generic: they may open the dialog and return the user's choice, but must not branch on effect classes or display types. Put attack-specific preview values on the attack effect and compose them with the effect's own bonus in the concrete modifier effect; see `.junie/guidelines/effects-guide.md`.
- For “set remaining life to N,” use a generic set-life effect rather than simulating it with healing; derive damage from effective maximum hit points so the resulting remaining life is exactly N.
- In reusable effects, do not branch on specific `TARGET_*` selectors or nested effect types to special-case callers. Pass the configured target through the normal resolver, preserve its result order, and apply only the configured filters; with no filter, keep the resolved targets unchanged.
- Preserve an ability's initiating character/controller for its full resolution, snapshotting that context before paying arrow costs. A cost may discard the ability's source card; this must not prevent the remaining effect from resolving. Do not keep the card in play artificially, and save any source-card values needed after payment before the cost removes it. Add a regression test for a self-discarding source.
- Read only the files relevant to the task; do not assume a guideline or specification that you have not checked.
- If guidance or documentation leaves an important behavior ambiguous, ask before making a consequential design choice.
